t: You're looking at a bronze statue of Benjamin Disraeli, on the west side of Parliament Square. It was unveiled in 1883 and is now Grade II listed. The sculptor was Mario Raggi, an Italian who settled in England and received several public commissions for statues of civic figures. Disraeli twice served as Prime Minister, and he's remembered for shaping the modern Conservative Party and for his one-nation conservatism. He's also remembered for his political battles with the Liberal leader Gladstone. Here, he stands looking out over the square, close to the Parliament where those battles were fought.
